claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy exhibits limited strain hardening.
The as-cast alloy exhibits poor deformation uniformity and rapid failure at high strain rates.
Pre-straining followed by tailored annealing, or dynamic thermomechanical processing, will generate a dense nano-twinned structure.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will increase the density of stacking faults.
Nano-twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the material.
A hierarchical twin network can provide pathways for dislocation glide and cross-slip along intersecting twin-boundary–matrix interfaces.
Stacking faults provide enhanced cross-slip and dislocation-transfer pathways in the treated HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy.
Stacking faults can make a significant contribution to strain hardening.
The nano-twin and stacking-fault mechanisms will sustain strain hardening and delay strain localization during adiabatic dynamic loading.
The treated alloy will have greater uniform plastic deformation and later initiation of localization than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will have higher dynamic yield and compressive strength than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will absorb more impact-induced energy than the as-cast baseline.
The predicted benefits apply under adiabatic loading above approximately 10^3 s^-1 and may not apply under low-rate or thermally non-adiabatic loading.

A matched test will compare as-cast and thermomechanically treated specimens under identical high-rate adiabatic loading while measuring strength, hardening, localization, energy absorption, and post-mortem microstructure.

The hypothesis is falsified if the treated specimens show no statistically significant improvement in dynamic strain hardening, uniform deformation, localization delay, and energy absorption relative to the as-cast controls.
